headline: Marsh clients saw 105 cyber incidents in late October, more than two-fold late May
body: Marsh said its clients saw 105 cyber incidents in the second half of October, more than two-fold the 48 recorded in the last two weeks of May. Marsh's Meredith Schnur said "we could attribute AI to a significant number of these". GlobalData, cited by Reuters, expects global cyber insurance premiums to rise to $18.3 billion in 2027.
note: GlobalData, as cited by Reuters, projects premium growth to accelerate to 10% in 2027.

evidence.text: Marsh said its clients saw 105 cyber incidents in the second half of October, a more than two-fold increase from the 48 recorded in the last two weeks of May.
Meredith Schnur , Marsh Risk’s U.S. and Canada cyber practice leader, said in an interview with Reuters.
So I would say we could attribute AI to a significant number of these.

Reuters cited findings from GlobalData showing that cyber insurance premiums are projected to grow at a faster pace over the next two years world wide as businesses respond to increasing attack frequency.
It expects global cyber insurance premiums to increase 6.9% to $16.6 billion this year, before accelerating to 10% growth for 2027 to $18.3 billion.
